edits.old: if (typeof input !== 'object' || input === null) return undefined;

expected_unnoticed: neither half of this guard is observable through the function's only call path, measured rather than assumed. `inProgressTodoText` has exactly one caller, `deriveStatus` (liveStatus.ts:176), and it skips any entry whose `toolInput === undefined`. A wire `tool_call` carrying `input: null` is normalized to `toolInput: undefined` by TurnReducer -- probed directly -- so NULL CAN NEVER ARRIVE HERE, and the `input === null` half has no reachable input. For every non-null primitive the remaining path reaches the identical `undefined` one line later: a string, a number and a boolean all have no `.todos`, so producer 2's `!Array.isArray(todos)` refuses them. L1-and-the-caller-filter-jointly is what pins the pair, and it IS caught. This declaration goes stale the moment `inProgressTodoText` gains a second caller, or `deriveStatus` stops filtering `toolInput === undefined`, or TurnReducer starts preserving a null tool input.

describes: producer 1 narrowed: null is admitted while other primitives are still rejected. The B shape -- the guard still fires for most inputs, so only the null case changes and producer 2 covers it

producer 2 loosened to a truthiness test: a non-empty string `todos` passes the guard and is iterated character by character, so a wire blob spelling todos as text yields a one-character status readout

producer 3 covered by a neighbour: `completed` is admitted alongside `in_progress`, so a finished list reports its last completed item as though it were live work
